draft.title: Fear of communism in Australia
card: Communism is a system in which the state owns most property and one party rules. In the Cold War, the United States and the Soviet Union were rivals, and many Australians feared communism would spread.
In Australia, some people feared communists would cause strikes and harm industry. Prime Minister Robert Menzies and his government wanted to act against the Communist Party of Australia.
In 1950 the government passed a law to ban the Communist Party. The High Court ruled the law invalid.
Menzies then asked voters to change the Constitution to allow a ban. At the referendum in 1951, a narrow majority of voters said No, so the party stayed legal.
draft.remember: Fear of communism led Menzies to try a ban, but voters rejected it in 1951.

a.q: What was the result of the 1951 referendum on banning the Communist Party?
opts: Voters rejected the change, so the party stayed legal
Voters accepted the change, so the party was banned
The High Court upheld the ban on the party
The referendum was cancelled before voters could vote
a.why: A narrow majority voted No, so the Constitution was not changed and the party was not banned. The High Court had already ruled the 1950 law invalid, so it had not upheld a ban.
a.clue: Think about whether the vote supported Menzies or not.

b.q: Why did Menzies hold a referendum in 1951 about the Communist Party?
opts: The High Court had ruled his ban law invalid
Voters had asked him to hold one after a strike
The Soviet Union had demanded a vote on the issue
The Constitution required a vote on every new law
b.why: After the High Court ruled the 1950 law invalid, Menzies tried to change the Constitution to give the government the power. Not every law needs a referendum, only changes to the Constitution.
b.clue: Think about what happened to the 1950 law before the referendum.

a.best: Voters rejected the change, so the party stayed legal

b.best: The High Court had ruled his ban law invalid
